Issued at 200 PM CDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Today and Tonight: Dangerous Heat and Severe Storms 

Low clouds have finally mixed out across much of the region with 
some mid/high clouds rounding the crest of the ridge. Even with 
these high clouds, many locations are already seeing early afternoon 
heat indices in the high 90s to around 105 with continued climbing 
expected through the duration of the afternoon. Dew points in the 
low to mid 80s have been observed over portions of Central Iowa this 
afternoon and southwest winds are slowly advecting this excessive 
moisture into Northeast Iowa and beyond. The Extreme Heat Warning 
will be in effect for most of the area until 9PM as dew points in 
the 70s to low 80s areawide will keep heat indices over the century 
mark well into the evening hours. 

Given the very warm and unstable airmass in place over the region, 
storms are expected to fire across portions of Northern 
Minnesota/Wisconsin in the vicinity of Lake Superior later today as 
a shortwave impulse rounds the ridge and starts to make its way 
southeast into the Upper Midwest/Great Lakes region. This looks to 
be the main focus for thunderstorm development but other weaker 
impulses across the Dakotas/Central Minnesota could set some storms 
off later this afternoon - though confidence in this scenario is 
lower given convective debris from residual storms out west for 
areas along the Minnesota/Iowa border. Forecast soundings across 
Central Wisconsin show ample instability with 2000+ J/kg of MUCAPE 
and 35-50 kts of effective shear just outside the periphery of the 
ridge. Initial supercells across Northern MN/WI are expected to grow 
upscale into more of an MCS type feature. Initial supercells would 
pose an all-hazards risk, though primarily large hail and damaging 
winds as 0-1 km shear and helicity is not looking overly 
favorable for tornadoes. Steep lapse rates aloft around 8 deg 
C/km would favor large hail growth but warm temperatures aloft 
might temper this risk overall. Winds look to be the main threat
with forecast DCAPE values between 1000-1500 J/kg. As we move 
through time and storms congeal into more of a cluster, wind 
will become the prevailing threat, especially as this looks to 
be happening into the evening/overnight hours where the 
inversion will start to set up and storms will start to become 
more elevated in nature. This cluster is expected to work its 
way south/southeast through Wisconsin into the overnight hours 
before moving off towards the Lake Michigan coastline.

Monday and Monday Night: Heat Risk Continues and Storm Potential 

Skies will start to clear out behind the remnants of the morning 
system and with dew points still in the 70s to low 80s across the 
region, heat indices are once again expected to climb to between 100-
110 for many tomorrow, with the warmest conditions expected across 
Northeast Iowa and Southwest Wisconsin. Locations further north and 
west across Southeast Minnesota will start to see a slight reprieve 
by the end of the day as a cold front starts to move through the 
region, shifting winds to the northwest around noon. Though ambient 
temperatures will still climb into the 90s for many, this will allow 
some slightly drier air to start to mix in from the northwest, which 
will start to fend off some of those upper 70s dew points, helping 
to lower those across Southeast Minnesota. The rest of us will 
unfortunately not feel the reprieve until Tuesday when temperatures 
are in the 80s and dew points are back in the 60s. 

Lingering activity from the overnight hours across West Central and 
Southwest Wisconsin could pose a marginal severe risk as it will be 
in an area of warm advection. The better lift will have passed with 
the shortwave impulse earlier but enough lingering instability will 
allow for a marginal hail and wind risk to persist into the morning 
hours for our far eastern zones. Overall concern later in the day 
tends to shift to the east as the upper trough and shortwave 
impulses take aim more at the Great Lakes/Michigan than western 
Wisconsin though some spotty showers and storms could pop up across 
Central/Southwestern Wisconsin tomorrow afternoon on the periphery 
of the ridge. Confidence in activity this far west tomorrow is much 
lower (around 20%) with most likely staying dry. 

Tuesday - Saturday: Warm Temperatures Continue with Storm Chances

The ridge shifts westward just enough and northwest flow remains in 
place. Both of these will mean temperatures cool down slightly, into 
the mid to upper 80s but it also means that the 70F dewpoints would 
be less likely to occur. Heat indices will also stay in the 80s to 
around 90F. With this flow pattern, ensemble guidance has low
